entries.title: No grey veil over the 3D track on a phone
entries.noswitch: the grey was a fault you found on the iPhone; there is nothing to switch back to
entries.look: On the iPhone simulator, the model, the land and the paper are their own colours again, not greyed. The grey came from the simulator's graphics chip, which can't read three.js's soft shadows and drew everything as if in shadow. The stage now checks for that once and falls back to plain shadows (harder shadow edges, only where the check fails; Chrome is pixel-for-pixel unchanged). A real iPhone probably never had the fault; not tested on a device. Drag, tap a section and press + and − quickly: the page doesn't zoom. Every 3D model on the site (Tracks, and both on a race page).

entries.title: The other drivers and When it went wrong, cleanly on a phone
entries.noswitch: the broken labels and the two-and-one year strips were faults you found; there is nothing to switch back to
entries.look: On the phone: every label under a number fits one line, no chevron on a line of its own ('In single-seaters', 'Cautions naming him' are the phone's shorter forms; the laptop keeps the full words). The INDY NXT seasons are one row a year, 2024, 2025, 2026, the year first, so the squares line up.

entries.title: INDY NXT: average finish, field beaten and top-ten rate three across
entries.noswitch: you asked for three across in place of two and one; the old wrap was the fault
entries.look: On the phone, the INDY NXT chapter's three numbers share one row in equal thirds, their numbers on one line; 'Field beaten, on average' takes two even lines above its number.

entries.title: Less white space above the footer, on every page
entries.noswitch: the empty band was a fault you found; the space is now the same gap as between the sections
entries.look: Scroll to the bottom of any page: the footer's rule sits one section gap under the last section (40 px on the phone, 72 px on the laptop and the Dell), where it was 140 and 136.
